Top events and screens show what your users do most. The daily chart tracks volume trends over the selected time window. All data is aggregated — no individual user is exposed.
Manage your projects and API keys. Each project has a unique API key — create separate projects for different apps, environments (dev/staging/prod), or platforms.
Toggle demo data for testing in debug mode. The demo switch only appears when the server runs in debug configuration. Production deployments hide this by default.

Screen transitions show how users navigate your app. Each row represents one common path from one screen to the next. High drop-off at a step may indicate UX friction — investigate why users leave at that point.

Retention shows what share of each cohort came back at least N days after their first launch. Each row is a weekly cohort; the shaded range under a percentage is its confidence interval — with a small cohort, treat the range as the honest answer, not the single number.

A funnel is an ordered list of events you already track, plus a time window. Each device evaluates its own progress and reports only how far it got — funnels are declared in your app's SDK config and appear here automatically once registered.

An experiment shows two versions of a screen or part of a screen to different devices and compares how often people interact with each. Assignment happens entirely on-device — QuietMetrix never knows which device saw which variant, only aggregate counts.
